tasks.short: Plan or adjust truck routes for changing conditions and fuel efficiency

steps.what: Read actual traffic changes, delivery requirements and current route information while safely stopped
Verify actual truck dimensions, load restrictions, delivery windows and remaining driving allowance
Transfer the current order's verified stops and constraints into the truck navigation planner
Compare navigation alternatives for practical access, distance, congestion and likely fuel use
Check the complete route, mapped stops and constraints, repairing unsupported or mismatched transfers
Activate the exact checked route on the truck navigation device

tasks.design: Test a native transfer from {OPS_SYSTEM} to {OTHER}, the truck navigation system, for the current order's stops and verified vehicle constraints. Remove that actual re-key only; retain route comparison, repair and final driver activation after the exact route is checked.
tasks.previous_blocker: Transport orders and navigation may require the driver to type the same stops and vehicle constraints twice.
tasks.enabler_now: An existing import interface or a small deterministic field mapping can transfer known order data into an inactive route draft.
tasks.still_hard: Road suitability, temporary restrictions and credible fuel trade-offs depend on actual vehicle and local conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The driver recognises an unsuitable approach even when a map offers it.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate destination entry while route responsibility stays with the driver and transport planner.

reach.task: Explain why a proposed truck route is unsuitable
reach.learn: Truck restrictions, delivery access and interpreting route alternatives

evidence.claim: A verified order-to-navigation field transfer can replace duplicate entry, but existing route calculation runtime is not saved driver labour. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: The focal role is a stopped truck driver adjusting a route in a workflow that actually re-keys order fields into a separate navigation system. This E1 case is not a claim that all fleets have ten hours of re-keying per hundred route-planning hours. No driving, fuel consumption or carbon reduction is converted into labour savings.

The transport planner already supplies order identifier, stop sequence, verified address or coordinates and delivery windows in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The fleet record supplies height, length, weight and vehicle restrictions; the driver verifies actual vehicle/load applicability and driving allowance in s2. Missing or ambiguous addresses or load restrictions stop transfer and require manual entry or planner clarification within s4-s5; no new clean planning feed is assumed.

s3 copies explicit fields into an inactive draft. Native navigation continues to calculate alternatives as today, with no runtime credit. s4 retains all practical comparison and route choice, and s5 retains nineteen hours for complete route meaning checks, stale-data rejection and manual transfer repair.

s5 binds final route geometry, stops, truck constraints and the exact truck device; any change voids s6 release. s6 is consequential route activation, not a gated ordinary save. No driver scoring or allocation by behaviour is introduced. Test the native interface before custom code; access and national employee consultation belong in rollout.
unknowns: Are order stops actually typed into navigation today?
Which truck constraints and stop fields can the installed navigation import?
How much exception repair occurs on foreign or restricted-access deliveries?
research_questions: Can an inactive native route draft preserve stop order and truck restrictions through an exact field transfer?

already_counted.description: Complete route review, mapped-stop checks and manual repair of unsupported transfers

incremental.description: Maintain order-to-navigation mappings and verify them after device or order-format changes

approvals.approved_version: Exact final route geometry, stops, vehicle/load constraints and truck navigation device checked in s5; edits or changed constraints invalidate release

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes ten duplicate-entry hours less one mapping upkeep hour: nine net. Cautious case: an unsupported navigation device requires manual entry, or the fleet already transfers stops; retain that current route without building another mapping or adding upkeep. Existing route calculation and all driver decisions remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inventory and inspect goods to establish actual quantities and condition

steps.what: Count and identify the actual goods against the consignment identities
Inspect packaging and visible goods condition, including relevant handling concerns
Enter actual quantities, units and condition observations into the existing load checklist
Compare recorded quantities and units with the manifest and identify exact discrepancies
Resolve uncertain counts, incompatible units and condition discrepancies manually
Save the existing factual load checklist without certifying acceptance or releasing a consignment

tasks.design: Configure an exact quantity-and-unit comparison in the existing {OPS_SYSTEM} load checklist. Keep physical counting, condition inspection, first capture and discrepancy repair human; the ordinary internal record save remains fully retained and ungated.
tasks.previous_blocker: The driver may compare manually entered counts against an already digital load manifest.
tasks.enabler_now: A native checklist rule can compare the same item identifiers and units after actual counts are entered.
tasks.still_hard: Mixed packages, unclear labels and damaged goods still need direct examination.
tasks.human_edge: The driver can recount a pallet and recognise damage a quantity rule cannot assess.
tasks.altitude: Less mechanical manifest comparison without changing responsibility for actual goods inspection.

reach.learn: Consignment identities, units of measure and neutral damage descriptions

evidence.claim: Exact comparison of entered counts and manifest quantities can be deterministic; it does not inspect goods or infer their condition. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: The focal role is the truck driver checking a consignment with an existing digital manifest and inspection checklist used for load reconciliation. No new trailing inspection register is invented. Shares are E1 scenario estimates; the current ten-hour manual comparison must be confirmed.

The shipper or warehouse supplies consignment identifier, item or handling-unit identifier, expected quantity and unit on the existing manifest. The driver actually counts and inspects in s1-s2 and types observed identifier, quantity, unit and condition in s3. Capture retains all fifteen hours; labels are not assumed to be automatically scanned.

s4 compares exact identifiers and same-unit quantities only. Missing identifiers, mixed units, partial packages and inaccessible goods stop comparison; s5 retains physical recounting, manual rule fallback and condition judgement. No condition classification, legal acceptance, signature, consignee notification or load-release action is automated.

Any actual contractual sign-off needs its own final-content approval and release workflow. s6 is only the author's ordinary internal factual save at a small fully retained one-percent share. Native comparison is tested first; existing automatic checks cannot earn a new labour benefit.
unknowns: Are expected and actual quantities currently compared manually?
Does the existing checklist already have comparison rules?
Are identifiers and units compatible for typical loads?
research_questions: Does the rule reject partial-package and unit mismatches while preserving the driver's actual condition observations?

already_counted.description: Manual discrepancy resolution, recounting and unsupported-unit fallback

incremental.description: Maintain supported quantity comparison rules and test manifest changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes ten manual comparison hours less one upkeep hour: nine net. Cautious case: mixed handling units or unlabeled goods prevent exact matching, so retain the whole manual comparison and do not deploy this rule. Physical examination, first data entry and the ordinary save remain in both cases.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Direct labourers packing goods and moving them onto trailers

steps.what: Read the available load plan and special handling instructions
Observe actual goods, trailer space and the loaders' current positions
Choose immediate packing and loading directions within the existing safe load plan
Give clear spoken directions to labourers and confirm that they understand
Watch the response and correct directions when actual loading conditions change

tasks.design: Retain the directly available load plan in {OPS_SYSTEM} and handling instructions in {DOCS}. Immediate loading directions remain spoken, with the driver watching actual movements and correcting them; no new written instruction packet is created.
tasks.previous_blocker: Directions respond to the physical loading scene and other people's immediate actions.
tasks.enabler_now: The existing plan supports the conversation, but a new document or model does not remove the need to direct and watch.
tasks.still_hard: Coordinating changing movements safely around a trailer.
tasks.human_edge: The driver sees misunderstanding and can stop or correct the movement immediately.
tasks.altitude: No change to the driver's work or authority from this design.

reach.task: Brief loaders on a safe immediate sequence
reach.learn: Clear signals, load stability and safe intervention

evidence.claim: A ready loading plan does not replace the driver's live direction and observation of actual loaders. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: The focal denominator is the driver's own direction time. Labourers' packing and carrying time is not included or credited. The planner or warehouse already provides the current load plan and special handling instructions; the driver reads them in s1 and produces the physical observations in s2.

The actual document lookup is split out and already directly available, so a native view creates no further saving in this case. No new signed loading brief, directive log or completion record is assumed for spoken directions. Actual consignment quantity and condition entry is separately explicit in task 10655, not hidden inside the conversation here.

Load-plan creation, signatures and contractual dispatch releases are not asserted as outcomes of these immediate directions. If local work contains an actual written instruction or dispatch send, it requires its own priced preparation and final release, rather than being treated as free.
No tool, structured feed or configuration is added, so additional upkeep is zero. Shares are provisional E1 estimates and no unchanged physical or spoken action is shortened.
unknowns: Do drivers issue any actual written loading directions beyond the current plan?
Is the loading plan already directly available at the trailer?
research_questions: Does observation reveal a repeated real instruction entry or send, rather than only immediate spoken guidance?

incremental.description: No new tool or ongoing upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All five document-reading hours and ninety-five live direction hours remain. The current plan is already available, and a new template would add an artefact without removing actual scene assessment, spoken instruction or watching the response.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce verified duplicate route entry and exact load-count comparison while preserving practical driving and loading judgement.
reach: Explain route-access constraints to a transport planner
Resolve a factual quantity mismatch with warehouse staff
role.ambitious_version: A driver with fewer duplicated planning fields and full attention retained for actual roads, goods and loading conditions.
